subject: Hosted API latency bands — rolling-window amendment request
messages:
From: Amelia Grant <amelia@fselect.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary adjustment to p95 measurement window during migration

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — F-Select is close to choosing a hosted inference partner and the SLO language is the last item the procurement team is probing. We have an upcoming ETL migration (June 20–27) that will cause predictable, high-variance traffic overnight as we backfill historical data. During a similar migration last year our p95 latency spiked for ~6 hours per night due to large batched requests, though p50 and overall user experience were unaffected.

Rather than sign a contract that immediately triggers SLA credits for that short window, would Redwood consider a time-limited rolling-window amendment: a two-week carveout that treats the nightly 4–7am PST window as a transient high-variance period and excludes those samples from the p95 calculation for the duration?

We can provide load traces and a short runbook if that helps. Our target is to avoid a formal SLA variance while the migration is in progress; we'd still expect p50 and normal daytime p95 to remain unchanged.

Appreciate a quick read — we need to get procurement comfortable before the 19th.

Thanks,
Amelia Grant
Director, Platform Engineering
F-Select Technologies

Attachments: fselect-load-patterns.csv (sample traces)
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Grant <amelia@fselect.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary adjustment to p95 measurement window during migration

Hi Amelia — thanks for the clear context and the traces. We can accommodate a short-term arrangement, but there are a few guardrails we need to put in place so the SLO remains meaningful for both sides. Proposed approach: 

- Two-week rolling-window amendment covering nightly local window 04:00–07:00 PST (June 20–July 3).
- During that window we would exclude samples tagged as "migration-batch" from the p95 aggregation; p50 remains measured across all traffic.
- We require your ops team to add an HTTP header x-fselect-traffic: migration-batch for requests from migration jobs so we can reliably tag/partition the measurements.
- Evidence package: load traces + KV cache hit-rate snapshot + a short runbook describing the job cadence.
- Canary: we propose a 48-hour canary (June 20–22) where we monitor behavior and confirm the header tagging before the carveout goes live. If we see user-facing degradation outside the window, Redwood reserves the right to revoke the carveout early.

If that sounds reasonable I'll loop in our SRE/measurements lead to finalize the phrasing for the contract amendment and provide a one-page provisional window template.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: provisional-window-template.pdf
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: F-Select — rolling-window amendment request (requesting technical sign-off)

Connor, Lauren — forwarding the request from F-Select (summary below). They want a two-week exclusion of nighttime batch traffic from p95 while preserving p50. They'll tag requests with x-fselect-traffic: migration-batch. Can you review and confirm the measurement mechanics and any risk to the hosted measurement pipeline? Highlights: 

- Window: 04:00–07:00 PST nightly, June 20–July 3
- Exclusion: requests with header x-fselect-traffic:migration-batch excluded from p95 calculation only
- Canary: 48-hour monitoring period prior to full carveout

Key questions:
- Is it feasible to partition and exclude by header reliably in our metrics backend for a short-lived rule?
- Any downstream implications for sampling, KV cache accounting, or billing?

I attached their load traces. Hope to keep this lightweight — procurement wants the amendment language by Friday.

Thanks,
Tessa

--- Forwarded message attached below for context ---
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 10:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: F-Select — rolling-window amendment request (requesting technical sign-off)

Tessa — quick notes from the measurements/serving side: 

- Partition by header is straightforward for a short-lived rule; we can apply an aggregation-time filter that omits samples with the tag in the p95 pipeline. We'll want to scope this to the F-Select tenant id to avoid accidental cross-tenant exclusions.
- Impact on sampling: if we exclude those requests from p95 only, sampling for p50 and other metrics remains unchanged. We'll need to ensure the sampling reservoir still gets a representative mix for day metrics.
- KV cache accounting: large batch jobs may have low cache hit rates; exclude-from-p95 is fine, but please capture a KV cache hit-rate snapshot from F-Select during the canary so we can confirm cache behavior.
- Billing: no change to billing; tokens are still charged.

I'll prepare the quick playbook we use for temporary measurement rules and attach a supporting CSV with the spot-checks I ran against their traces. If procurement needs a one-line clause we can offer: "Redwood and F-Select agree to a temporary, tenant-scoped measurement amendment to exclude migration-tagged traffic from p95 aggregation for the defined window; all other SLOs remain in force."

Connor
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachment: kv-cache-evidence.csv
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Grant <amelia@fselect.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary adjustment to p95 measurement window during migration

Hi Amelia — good news. We've reviewed the traces and Connor confirmed the measurement-side changes are low-risk. Redwood can offer a two-week, tenant-scoped rolling-window amendment with the following conditions: 

1) Window: nightly 04:00–07:00 PST, June 20–July 3.
2) Exclusion mechanism: requests must include header x-fselect-traffic: migration-batch. Redwood will exclude those requests from p95 aggregation only; p50 remains measured across all traffic.
3) Canary: June 20–22 (48 hours). F-Select will tag traffic for the canary; Redwood will monitor real-user latency and cache metrics. If we detect user-facing impact outside the window we will pause the carveout.
4) Evidence: please upload the canary load traces and a KV cache hit-rate snapshot to the HubSpot deal (link below) before 06:00 PST on June 20.
5) Documentation: we'll send a one-page amendment for signature. This will be a temporary operational amendment (no change to pricing or baseline SLAs) and will automatically expire July 3 unless extended in writing.

Next steps: can you confirm the header tagging plan and upload the evidence to HubSpot? Once confirmed we'll push the provisional amendment doc and schedule a short monitoring kickoff (30 minutes) on June 20 at 03:45 PST.

Doc link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DEAL-78934
Template: https://docs.redwood.com/slo/rolling-window-template

Thanks — looking forward to wrapping this quickly.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
